::: {#def-tensor}

#### Tensor

A **tensor** is an array of numbers arranged on a regular grid with any number of dimensions [@goodfellow2016deep, section 2.1].
Every entry is picked out by one index per dimension.

A tensor with no dimensions is a scalar,
one with one dimension is a vector,
and one with two is a matrix.
PyTorch says "dimensions" (`ndim`, and `dim=` in its functions),
where NumPy, which also says `ndim`, calls them "axes" (`axis=`);
other sources say "modes", or call the number of dimensions the tensor's "order" or "rank".
That "rank" is not the rank of a matrix.
Physics and mathematics use "tensor" for a multilinear map,
which an array of numbers represents once a basis is chosen;
[deep learning](course-overview.qmd#def-deep-learning) means only the array.

:::
